Subject: Amendment request — additional capacity for Nov + retro billing

Hi Markus,

Hope you’re well — we pushed a pilot into production earlier this month and the usage spiked unexpectedly. We need to add 80k token-equivalent capacity for November and would like to get an amendment in place that:

- Captures the additional committed capacity (80k) starting 2026-11-01,
- Applies retroactive prorated billing for November usage, and
- Locks the current rate ladder for the term so we don’t float to next quarter pricing during renewal.

I’ve attached a short CSV with the November usage by environment (usage_report_nov.csv). Procurement would like a proposed commercial term sheet we can circulate to finance by Monday. Can you loop in legal for a quick review of the back-dated effective date?

Thanks,
Sam

Folks — attaching a proposed fee ladder and commercial note (proposed_fee_ladder.xlsx). Summary below:

- Add 80k token commitment for Nov 2026 (retroactive effective 2026-11-01)
- Apply a prorated charge for Nov based on actual usage vs. committed volume; any overages beyond the new commit billed at the overage rate defined in Exhibit A
- Lock current discounted rate tiers through the end of the existing term (2027-02-28)
- No change to SLA; we will provide burst capacity for sustained spikes during onboarding window (Nov 1–Dec 31)

Lauren — noted question for legal: procurement prefers the amendment to explicitly state the retroactive effective date and the proration formula. Please mark any problematic language in the attached draft amendment (I’ll upload a DOCX after legal comments).

Karthik

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Proposed fee ladder + proration approach for Nexa Health (legal redlines)

Team / Sam — I reviewed the commercial proposal and attached a redlined amendment (Redwood_Amendment_v1_redlines.pdf). High-level notes:

1) Retroactive effective date: we can accept backdating to 2026-11-01, but we need a clause that clarifies that billing adjustments are limited to usage records supplied by the customer and reconciled within 45 days of invoice issuance. This prevents open-ended audit exposures.

2) Proration formula: suggest we apply proration at the consolidated account level by default; if Nexa requires per-environment line items, we should explicitly state invoice line-itemization and include a short sample calculation in Exhibit B.

3) Rate lock: legal is fine with locking the agreed rate tiers through 2027-02-28, but recommend adding an exception for forced security or compliance upgrades that materially increase costs (standard carve-out).

4) Sign-off path: we need procurement and finance countersignatures and a single DocuSign envelope — please confirm the signer list.

Sam — I attached the PDF redline and a clean Word we can finalize. Note two minor editorial edits in clauses 2.3 and 4.1 that Karthik should confirm — I left comments in the DOCX.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
